knowledge_gaps: The symmetric distance penalty encourages proximity to each query, not globally recent items. Only the terminal MASK directly favors recent history; interior queries favor nearby items on both sides. Its connection to stale-interest failures therefore needs sharper justification.

The initialization may make the intervention negligible: softplus(-4) is approximately 0.018, so the largest initial penalty is approximately 0.018 logits, and the parameter gradient is also attenuated. Learning-rate treatment, weight decay and monitoring of learned strengths are unspecified.

Reproducibility remains incomplete without integration into the actual baseline, predictor writer and diagnostic adapter. A zero-bias version of the replacement attention path should first reproduce baseline scores, separating locality effects from attention implementation changes.

Originality assessment omits KERPLE, whose logarithmic relative-position bias is a particularly close precedent. Potential 7/10 remains speculative without measured history sensitivity; implementation difficulty also depends on whether additive masks disable efficient attention kernels.

The experimental plan lacks a concrete budget allocation, mandatory matched control and prespecified checkpoint comparison. Historical scores cannot isolate locality effects. Track terminal and interior behavior separately, history-length effects, MASK self-attention and degradation on durable interests; paired uncertainty estimates require existing host per-user outcomes.
